body: We loved it! Solo Mio is a wonderful story with interesting twists! The movie is filled with Laughs, tears, some silliness, surprise appearances, and, you will leave with a huge smile! The unique cast of characters is great fun! We Enjoyed the beautiful travel log of various parts of Italy as well! Go see it, you will be so pleasantly surprised!

LIKES: Acting The Scenery/Setting The Sound Editing The Tasteful Comedy Beautiful Messaging Engaging Character Development A Nice Little Twist Authentic The Music Is Fun Moves At A Good Pace

Summary: Solo Mio is a film all about the message, characters, and a deeper meaning that Hollywood knows how to sell in their artistry. Helping to bring much of what I will be talking about to life is the acting, a film that stretches some talents into a serious range I've not seen in some time. James is delightful with his vulnerabilities, taking the normally klutzy, naïve doofus role, and transforming it into a likeable, lovable human who is relatable as we sort of live vicariously in his adventure. He portrays the emotions with a balance I've not seen before, and I found the performance charming, relatable, and quite honestly, one of his best characters I've seen from him. His buddies played by Roumie and Coates are okay, alongside the significant others; they provide this attempt at comedic relief that struck a chord with people in my showing. They deliver some sage moments, but they feel a bit more cartoony and overexaggerated to help break a bit of the drama up and keep the fun times going in the plot and mood. Yet, Nicole Grimaudo was the other actor that I became enchanted with. A solid character in the role of Gia, her character is a bit more dynamic, playing all states of the emotional spectrum, and playing well with everyone. Between her elegant beauty, grounded modality, and this deeper level of understanding humanity, Grimaudo brings so much of the movie together to be a centerpiece worth watching this film for, embracing much of what I'm about to talk about.

Past the performances, the movie is not reinventing the wheel in terms of new techniques, styles, or even creative worlds it is building. What it does do is capture so much of the movie's down-to-earth tones and realism, but puts this artistic finish on it as well. Solid camera work brings to life an amazing scenery, capturing the Italian city lifestyle as if we are walking through the town. Plenty of well-placed shots, good use of the locations, and using so much of the European natural vibes help you escape the world's problems and take a fake vacation to this land, which I enjoyed falling into. The sound components are also solid, conversations are easy to understand and mostly even, and all the natural noises of life are blended well. This is true for the music, where Italian artists give us their original works or twists to familiar tunes, all well-utilized with their planning to bring an extra vibe to the scene or sequence. It's a lot of fun, and the theater really helps to filter out so much and immerse you in all that Angel Studios was trying to offer with this movie.

But despite what sounds like typical admiration in my reviews, Solo Mio's other strength is just the depth of this film. As we traverse the country, Matt's story is not so much brought to life in a dragged-out drama as it is about learning to process what happened and slowly beginning to heal. It's done through character development and this cute aesthetic, a planned Honeymoon that brings him into unlikely company, and using Italy's world and culture to learn. There are fun little dives into the tourism, and in these moments, in varying levels of beauty, joy, hurt, and life, all mixed in a balanced manner. There is tasteful comedy (at times) to mix things up, helping to keep the movie from being monotone and predictable, but I never felt super insulted by any jokes or found any major rudeness, despite my disagreement with their approaches. Still, the whole thing is fun, moving at an approachable pace that tries condense all of this into a manageable time. And the authenticity to all of it helps to make the messages even stronger, circumventing the cheesy moments that so many films preach to a fault. Add a nice little twist to the film, and this tale turns out to be a much better film than I anticipated.

DISLIKES: Other Characters Are A Bit Too Stupid It's A Bit Uneven In The Adventures Slow A Few Times The Ending Feels A Bit Rushed/Preachy My showing Sound Levels Were Off

Summary: However, there are still some elements I had wished been a bit ironed out. One of the things that annoyed me was the character utilization and design for most of the secondary cast. So many of Matt's fellow vacationers are a bit too much at times, spouting a lot of idiotic nonsense that might appeal to certain goers. They are very exaggerated, in your face, and I didn't find them that funny when they failed to balance that out with something more meaningful. Their partners, as well, offered some potential, but they too fell into the same level of silliness that is good for a laugh, but not much more. I found them distracting, and would have liked a little more connection, growth, and wow factor that Gia brought with her stories. The adventures are also a tad uneven. There were times we barely touched on the adventure of the city, and other times we dove right into the cultural facets that seem to be accurate to the Italian way of life. I didn't feel any were wasted, but the unbalanced time in them led to some uneven storytelling and disappointed me to lose the story we were building, including the pacing, a few times getting a bit slow. Where I felt the movie lost some of the authenticity the most was in the ending. As much as I enjoyed what they did, the ending feels like a bow tied on quickly to wrap things up, happening at a much faster speed, which then tries to wrap things. While I got the gist of it, there was some information, running jokes, and cheesiness that felt divergent from the natural times. It's not that I hate those movements, but when you have such a beautiful film, to do it at the end feels like a cop out. Finally, the sound editing is also off-kilter, the music booming loudly in my theater before it returned to the balanced tones. It's minor, but I try to cover as much as I can.

The VERDICT: Angel Studios broadened their horizons, and in my opinion, it's a great direction that blends their philosophy, but puts it in a less preachy tale. In this case, Solo Mio is an authentic adventure that holds so much natural flavor in storytelling, feeling, setting, and character development. It's charming, with relatable characters and character issues to grab onto and potentially gain some assistance with healing and growth. The movie has a well-balanced pace, should be appealing to a wide variety, and does feel like a nice escape that isn't too overbearing, slow, or preachy to pull all that investment out from under you. True, there are going to be large swaths of the younger audience who this might not appeal to, given the targeted group. And for me, the secondary characters are misused and a bit too silly to fit naturally in this film, or provide the same amazing chemistry that the leads do. Throw in moments that stir up the natural feeling, and some other small limitations, and I think you'll find that this movie is not going to be for a family outing until your kids are in their late teens or early adult lives. Still, all in all, I'm very happy with this movie and encourage date nights, soul-searchers, church groups, and other young adults and upwards to check it out in theaters if you can.

My scores for Solo Mio are: Comedy/Romance: 8.0-8.5 Movie Overall: 7.5-8.0.

This was such a refreshing couples movie - the kind you finish and immediately feel lighter. The writing was thoughtful and engaging without being complicated, and it managed to stay genuinely funny and heartfelt at the same time. Best of all, it didn't rely on crude humor or foul language to keep your attention, which made it easy to just relax and enjoy the story.

The actors had wonderful chemistry and made their characters feel real and likable. You actually find yourself rooting for them instead of rolling your eyes at predictable moments. The pacing was just right - never slow, never chaotic - and the story stayed sweet without becoming cheesy.

It's the perfect movie for a date night or a cozy evening together. Fun, warm, and uplifting - the kind of film that reminds you why simple, well-told love stories still work.

Highly recommend if you want something entertaining and feel-good without being over the top.

Kevin James was great and the supporting cast were all good. I enjoyed watching Jonathan Roumie in a completely different role. The story was believable and the humor organic. There were a few surprises as well. This film really showed the beauty of Italy and the warmth of the culture. It was a warm and funny movie. I'd see it again.

My husband even enjoyed it! The first thing he said when the movie ended...."That was really good, I enjoyed it." I agreed.

This was a very good movie full of love, laughter, loss, turmoil, heartbreak and hope all wrapped in some great humor. Relationships started from curiosity grew into genuine caring.

We left with smiles...worth the watch!!!
